item.title: Welcome to the New Era of Video Game Adaptations
item.description: Buckle up, because that trend is about to kick into full gear. This week, we got a flood of news stories confirming that Hollywood is in a full-on gold rush. The film rights to video games are currently getting snapped up at an alarming rate. While that’s not exactly new for an industry that has a long history of eyeing game movies that never pass the scripting phase, we’re actually seeing significant developments that signal an approaching tidal wave.

item.title: 20 Years Later, The Departed's Best Line Is Still One Of The Greatest Quotes In Gangster Movie History
item.description: In crime cinema, a lethal line of dialogue can carry just as much weight as a loaded gun. Martin Scorsese's Goodfellas hooks audiences with Henry Hill's seductive declaration, “As far back as I can remember, I always wanted to be a gangster,” framing a life of crime as the ultimate aspiration. Miller's Crossing features Tom Reagan's wonderfully blunt take on underworld survival, while Casino , Scarface , and The Godfather overflow with dialogue that has long since bled into the cultural lexicon. Immortal phrases like “keep your friends close, but your enemies closer” and “an offer you can’t refuse” remain cinematic icons right alongside the actors and directors who brought them to life.

item.title: Forget Jason Statham, the Best Action Movie of the Last 30 Years Is Back on Netflix
item.description: Harrison Ford spent decades making wildly implausible heroes feel like ordinary guys having a terrible day. An archaeologist outrunning a giant boulder? Sure. A space smuggler taking on an evil empire? Absolutely. In Air Force One , he pulls off something that now feels considerably more farfetched: an American president you’d trust with your life.

item.title: 24 Years Later, the Funniest Lord of the Rings Movie Quote Is Still a Legendary Fantasy Line
item.description: Somewhere in Middle-earth, is there a Chili’s that serves orcs? Does an Uruk-hai host greet hungry customers, tell them it’ll be a 20-minute wait, and hand them a menu? Does the kitchen run out of manflesh halfway through the dinner rush? Is halfling served as an appetizer? What precisely is in the Triple Dipper? These are unreasonable questions to ask of an otherwise perfect fantasy epic. Unfortunately, The Lord of the Rings : The Two Towers invites every one of them with one line that feels deeply anachronistic.

item.title: 9 Years Later, Jon Bernthal’s Action Series Is a Masterpiece From Start to Finish
item.description: Ever since superhero movies and television became popular, fans have debated which actors are the perfect fit for their characters. The debate has escalated over the years, especially when multiple actors have played iconic characters like Superman and Spider-Man . Nine years ago, one of the best actor-to-character pairings came when Jon Bernthal took on Frank Castle in The Punisher . In the process, Bernthal delivered one of the grittiest and most action -packed comic book adaptations in history.

item.title: Ridley Scott's Near-Perfect Sci-Fi Masterpiece is Waiting to Be Rediscovered on Streaming
item.description: The ‘70s and ‘80s was a major turning point for science fiction . Star Wars revitalized the genre in 1977 and turned it into one of Hollywood’s main box office draws, inspiring a wave of films that reshaped the entire industry. Two years later, Ridley Scott threw down the gauntlet with Alien , taking a big step away from the optimism that had once permeated sci-fi pulp storytelling and instead infusing it with corporate anxiety and untrustworthy artificial intelligence. It was a signal for things to come.

item.title: All 8 Dungeon Crawler Carl Books Ranked (by Their Goodreads Score)
item.description: Matt Dinniman's Dungeon Crawler Carl takes one of fantasy's oldest setups and throws it into a blender with reality television, apocalyptic horror, and video game logic, creating a series that has evolved into one of the biggest breakout hits in modern speculative fiction. The premise is fairly simple, starting with a fight for survival inside an alien-dominated game show that escalates into a sprawling saga of bizarre monsters, convoluted mechanics, and a talking cat with an ego to match.

item.title: Patrick Stewart's Perfect 'Simpsons' Episode Reveals the Beloved Actor's Secret Weapon
item.description: Yesterday, news broke that Sir Patrick Stewart died at age 86. With his background performing Shakespeare and his incredible sense of dignity and gravitas, Stewart is being celebrated primarily for his work as Captain Jean-Luc Picard on Star Trek: The Next Generation , as well as being the perfect man to portray Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films. But while he was beloved for the dramatic weight he brought to his roles, it's worth acknowledging that the man pulled off some incredibly memorable comedic performances, one of the first was on The Simpsons , where he guest-starred in the season 6 episode, “Homer the Great.”

item.title: 10 Video Games With the Best Twist Endings Nobody Saw Coming
item.description: The best twist endings in video games change what you thought you were playing. A great one makes you want to start over to spot the clues, and a perfect one hides those clues in plain sight: in dialogue, in chapter titles, perhaps even the controller you’re holding. These ten games span three decades and nearly every genre, from horror to puzzle-platformers to a Game Boy adventure about a dream. But they all have one thing in common: Every one of them had us totally fooled the first time.

item.title: Andy Weir's New Time-Travel Sci-fi Thriller Officially Arrives Nov. 5
item.description: Andy Weir is known for combining humor, hard science fiction , and gripping survival stories in his bestselling novels The Martian and Project Hail Mary , which were both adapted into blockbuster films. He’s sticking to that formula for his next project, a time-travel thriller that will launch on Audible on Nov. 5.
